entry.title: Jev Ultrafast: The Sub-10-Second Web Agent Architecture
entry.summary:
Autonomous web agents represent one of the most promising frontiers of modern artificial intelligence. However, developers who have deployed browser agents in production quickly encounter a severe constraint: excessive latency and prohibitive token costs.
The prevailing industry pattern—often referred to as "Computer Use" or vision-based browsing—relies on a brute-force approach: Render the browser viewport to a full-resolution PNG image. Send image buffers across the network to a frontier multimodal model. Wait several seconds for the model to predict spatial $(x, y)$ coordinate clicks. Execute the click, wait for page mutations, and repeat the cycle. entry.title: DEV Challenge 1 Complete - StudyMate
entry.summary:
This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Weekend Challenge: Build for a Friend StudyMate is an AI-powered study companion built for students who spend too much time converting long study material into something they can actually revise. I built it with fellow students in mind — especially when exams are approaching and there is a lot of material to go through. StudyMate allows a student to paste their study material and automatically generates: 📝 Concise study notes 🔑 Important key points 🧠 AI-generated multiple-choice questions ✅ Interactive quizzes with instant scoring Instead of manually reading through lengthy material and creating revision notes and questions, StudyMate turns the material into a structured revision experience in seconds.
💻 GitHub Repository: https://github.com/ShouryaShinde/StudyMate The project is organized as a monorepo containing: client/ — React + Vite frontend packages/ui/ — Shared shadcn/ui components server/ — Node.js + Express backend Ollama integration for local AI inference StudyMate is built around open-source AI and local inference. Frontend React TypeScript Vite Tailwind CSS shadcn/ui React Router Backend Node.js Express.js Ollama AI Model llama3.2:3b The core AI functionality runs through Ollama locally rather than relying on a proprietary hosted AI API. When a student submits study material, the frontend sends it to the Express backend: Student ↓ Study Material ↓ React Frontend ↓ Express API ↓ Ollama ↓ Llama 3.2 3B ↓ Structured JSON ↓ Notes + Key Points + Quiz
